```{r}
font_add_google("Open Sans")
showtext_auto()

# Define theme_reason based on the uploaded file
theme_reason <- function(base_line_size = 0.5,
                         base_family = "Open Sans",
                         base_size = 12) {
  theme_minimal(base_family = base_family,
                base_size = base_size,
                base_line_size = base_line_size) %+replace%
    theme(
      axis.ticks = element_line(),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey92"),
      legend.position = "top"
    )
}

C1 <- "#CC0100"  # Light orange
```

```{r}
df <- read.csv("all_plans_2023.csv")

# Combine returns into a new column 'return', prioritizing 'market_return_from_valuation' over 'market_return_from_acfr'
df <- df %>%
  mutate(return = ifelse(!is.na(market_return_from_valuation), market_return_from_valuation, market_return_from_acfr))

# Clean the data: Keep relevant columns and remove rows with missing return values
df_clean <- df %>%
  select(Name, FY, return) %>%
  filter(!is.na(return))

# Ensure FY is numeric
df_clean$FY <- as.numeric(df_clean$FY)
df_clean$return <- as.numeric(df_clean$return)

# Calculate the average return per year
average_returns <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(FY) %>%
  summarize(average_return = mean(return, na.rm = TRUE))

# Plotting using ggplot2
ggplot() +
  # Plot returns for each plan
  geom_line(data = df_clean, aes(x = FY, y = return, group = Name, color = Name), alpha = 0.3) +  
  # Plot the average return line
  geom_line(data = average_returns, aes(x = FY, y = average_return), color = "black", size = 1.2) +
  # Add titles and labels
  labs(title = "Annual Returns for Each Plan and Average Return by Year",
       x = "Fiscal Year", y = "Return") +
  theme_reason() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")


```

```{r}
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(Name) %>%
  arrange(FY) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_return = cumsum(return) * 100)  # Convert cumulative returns to percentages

# Separate Nevada PERS from other plans
nevada_pers <- df_clean %>% filter(grepl("Nevada Public Employees Retirement System", Name))
other_plans <- df_clean %>% filter(!grepl("Nevada Public Employees Retirement System", Name))

# Calculate the average cumulative return per year
average_cumulative_returns <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(FY) %>%
  summarize(average_cumulative_return = mean(cumulative_return, na.rm = TRUE))

# Plot the data
NPERS <- ggplot() +
  # Plot other plans in the background
  geom_line(data = other_plans, aes(x = FY, y = cumulative_return, group = Name), color = "gray", alpha = 0.5) +
  # Highlight Nevada PERS
  geom_line(data = nevada_pers, aes(x = FY, y = cumulative_return), color = "red", size = 1.2) +
  # Add black line for average cumulative return
  geom_line(data = average_cumulative_returns, aes(x = FY, y = average_cumulative_return), color = "black", size = 1.2, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Comparison of Nevada PERS vs. Other Pension Plans",
       x = "Fiscal Year", y = "Cumulative Return (%)") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1)) +  # Format y-axis as percentage
  xlim(2002, 2022) +  # Cut off the graph at 2022
  theme_reason()  # Apply the custom Reason theme

print(NPERS)
# Save the plot to the 'outputs' folder with adjusted size to match R preview
ggsave("outputs/nevada_pers_comparison_percentage.png", plot = NPERS, width = 12, height = 8)


```


```{r}

df_diff_returns <- read_xlsx("DiffReturns.xlsx")

# Convert the returns to cumulative growth (multiplying cumulative returns)
df_diff_returns <- df_diff_returns %>%
  mutate(`Nevada PERS Cumulative` = cumprod(1 + `Nevada PERS`),
         `Montgomery County Cumulative` = cumprod(1 + `Montgomery County`),
         `Butler County Cumulative` = cumprod(1 + `Butler County`),
         `Harvard Cumulative` = cumprod(1 + Harvard))

# Filter the df_clean data to get cumulative growth for all funds from 2013 to 2022
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  filter(FY >= 2013 & FY <= 2022) %>%
  group_by(Name) %>%
  arrange(FY) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_return = cumprod(1 + return) - 1)  # Convert to cumulative growth

# Calculate the average cumulative growth for each year for all funds
average_cumulative_growth <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(FY) %>%
  summarize(average_cumulative_return = mean(cumulative_return, na.rm = TRUE))

# Plotting the cumulative growth for Nevada PERS, Montgomery County, Butler County, Harvard, and the average cumulative growth
harvard <- ggplot(df_diff_returns, aes(x = fye)) +
  # Add lines for each entity
  geom_line(aes(y = `Nevada PERS Cumulative`, color = "Nevada PERS"), size = 1.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = `Montgomery County Cumulative`, color = "Montgomery County"), size = 1.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = `Butler County Cumulative`, color = "Butler County"), size = 1.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = `Harvard Cumulative`, color = "Harvard"), size = 1.2) +
  # Add a line for the average cumulative growth of all funds
  geom_line(data = average_cumulative_growth, aes(x = FY, y = average_cumulative_return, color = "Average All Funds"), size = 1.2, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "10-Year Cumulative Growth (2013 to 2022)",
       x = "Fiscal Year", y = "Cumulative Growth (%)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2013, 2022, by = 1), labels = as.character(seq(2013, 2022, by = 1))) +  # Only show whole years
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1)) +  # Format y-axis as percentage
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Nevada PERS" = "#FF6733", "Montgomery County" = "#2779CB", "Butler County" = "#F6B941", "Harvard" = "#A51C30", "Average All Funds" = "black")) +
  theme_reason() +  # Apply custom Reason theme
  xlim(2013, 2022)  # Cut off the graph at 2022

print(harvard)

```

```{r}
# Calculate geometric means for Nevada PERS, Montgomery County, Butler County, and Harvard
geometric_mean_10_years <- df_diff_returns %>%
  filter(fye != 2023) %>%  # Exclude year 2023
  summarize(
    Nevada_PERS_Geometric = (prod(1 + `Nevada PERS` / 100)^(1/10) - 1) * 100,
    Montgomery_County_Geometric = (prod(1 + `Montgomery County` / 100)^(1/10) - 1) * 100,
    Butler_County_Geometric = (prod(1 + `Butler County` / 100)^(1/10) - 1) * 100,
    Harvard_Geometric = (prod(1 + Harvard / 100)^(1/10) - 1) * 100
  )

# Calculate the geometric mean for the average returns from the average_returns dataset (2013-2022)
average_returns_geometric <- average_returns %>%
  filter(FY >= 2013 & FY <= 2022) %>%
  summarize(
    Average_All_Plans_Geometric = (prod(1 + average_return / 100)^(1/10) - 1) * 100
  )

# Bind the geometric mean for all plans
geometric_mean_10_years <- geometric_mean_10_years %>%
  bind_cols(average_returns_geometric)

# Now, calculate the geometric mean for Pennsylvania PSERS and SERS from df
df_pennsylvania <- df %>%
  filter(Name %in% c("Pennsylvania Public School Employees' Retirement System", 
                     "Pennsylvania State Employees' Retirement System"),
         FY != 2023)  # Exclude year 2023

# Combine returns into a new column 'return', prioritizing 'market_return_from_valuation' over 'market_return_from_acfr'
df_pennsylvania <- df_pennsylvania %>%
  mutate(return = ifelse(!is.na(market_return_from_valuation), market_return_from_valuation, market_return_from_acfr)) %>%
  select(Name, FY, return) %>%
  filter(!is.na(return))

# Ensure FY and return columns are numeric
df_pennsylvania$FY <- as.numeric(df_pennsylvania$FY)
df_pennsylvania$return <- as.numeric(df_pennsylvania$return)

# Filter data for the last 10 years (2013-2022)
df_pennsylvania_10_years <- df_pennsylvania %>%
  filter(FY >= 2013 & FY <= 2022)

# Calculate the geometric mean for PSERS and SERS
geometric_mean_10_years_penn <- df_pennsylvania_10_years %>%
  group_by(Name) %>%
  summarize(geometric_mean = (prod(1 + return / 100)^(1/10) - 1) * 100)

# Bind the Pennsylvania plans' geometric means to the existing geometric_mean_10_years table
geometric_mean_10_years <- geometric_mean_10_years %>%
  bind_rows(geometric_mean_10_years_penn)

# Print the final table with geometric means for all plans
print(geometric_mean_10_years)


```

```{r}
df_clean2 <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(Name) %>%
  arrange(FY) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_return = cumprod(return) * 100)  # Convert cumulative returns to percentages

# Separate Nevada PERS from other plans
penn_states <- df_clean2 %>% filter(grepl("Pennsylvania Public School Employees' Retirement System", Name))%>% 
    mutate(cumulative_return = (cumprod(1 + return) - 1) * 100)
penn_teachers <- df_clean2 %>% filter(grepl("Pennsylvania State Employees' Retirement System", Name))%>%    
  mutate(cumulative_return = (cumprod(1 + return) - 1) * 100)

df_diff_filtered <- df_diff_returns %>%
  select(-`Nevada PERS`)

# Plotting the cumulative growth for Nevada PERS, Montgomery County, Butler County, Ohio STRS, and the average cumulative growth
Penn <- ggplot(df_diff_filtered, aes(x = as.numeric(fye))) +  # Ensure x-axis is numeric
  # Add lines for each entity
  geom_line(aes(y = `Montgomery County Cumulative` * 100, color = "Montgomery County"), size = 1.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = `Butler County Cumulative` * 100, color = "Butler County"), size = 1.2) +
  geom_line(data = penn_states, aes(x = FY, y = cumulative_return, color = "Penn State"), size = 1.8) +
  geom_line(data = penn_teachers, aes(x = FY, y = cumulative_return, color = "Penn Teachers"), size = 1.8) +
  geom_line(data = average_cumulative_growth, aes(x = FY, y = average_cumulative_return * 100, color = "Average All Funds"), size = 1.2, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "10-Year Cumulative Growth (2013 to 2022)",
       x = "Fiscal Year", y = "Cumulative Growth (%)") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2013, 2022, by = 1), labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 1)) +  # No decimal points on x-axis
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(scale = 1)) +  # Format y-axis with correct values multiplied by 100
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Montgomery County" = "#F6B941", "Butler County" = "#2779CB", "Penn State" = "#CC0100", "Penn Teachers" = "#2F456B", "Average All Funds" = "black")) +
  theme_reason() +  # Apply custom Reason theme
  theme(legend.title = element_blank()) +  # Remove "colour" from the legend title
  xlim(2013, 2022)  # Ensure the x-axis ends at 2022

# Print the plot
print(Penn)

```



# Ohio ! 

```{r}
# Filter the dataset for Ohio STRS
ohio_strs <- df_clean %>%
  filter(Name == "Ohio State Teachers Retirement System") %>%
  arrange(FY) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_return = cumprod(1 + return) - 1)  # Calculate cumulative growth for Ohio STRS

# Filter the data for the last 10 years
df_clean_10_years <- df_clean %>%
  filter(FY >= max(FY) - 9) %>%
  group_by(Name) %>%
  arrange(FY) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_return = cumprod(1 + return) - 1)  # Calculate cumulative growth for all funds

# Calculate the average cumulative growth per year for all public pension funds
average_cumulative_growth <- df_clean_10_years %>%
  group_by(FY) %>%
  summarize(average_cumulative_return = mean(cumulative_return, na.rm = TRUE))

# Plot cumulative growth for Ohio STRS and average public pension fund growth
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = df_clean_10_years, aes(x = FY, y = cumulative_return, group = Name), color = "gray", alpha = 0.5) +  # Other public pension funds
  geom_line(data = ohio_strs, aes(x = FY, y = cumulative_return), color = "blue", size = 1.2) +  # Ohio STRS
  geom_line(data = average_cumulative_growth, aes(x = FY, y = average_cumulative_return), color = "black", size = 1.2, linetype = "dashed") +  # Average of all plans
  labs(title = "10-Year Cumulative Growth of Ohio STRS vs. Aggregated Public Pension Funds",
       x = "Fiscal Year", y = "Cumulative Growth (%)") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(min(ohio_strs$FY), max(ohio_strs$FY), by = 1)) +
  theme_reason()

# Calculate the average returns for public pensions and Ohio STRS
average_return_public <- mean(average_cumulative_growth$average_cumulative_return, na.rm = TRUE)
average_return_ohio_strs <- mean(ohio_strs$cumulative_return, na.rm = TRUE)

# Display the average returns
cat("The average cumulative return for public pensions over the last 10 years is:", round(average_return_public * 100, 2), "%\n")
cat("The average cumulative return for Ohio STRS over the last 10 years is:", round(average_return_ohio_strs * 100, 2), "%\n")


```
